_comment: Pinned instance catalogue and price list. Prices live IN THE REPO, not fetched at analysis time.
Three reasons: an analysis run must be reproducible months later; a pricing-API outage must never
block a recommendation; and a savings figure in a merged PR has to still mean something when
somebody reads the PR next quarter. `as_of` is printed next to every rupee figure in the UI so a
stale catalogue is visible rather than silently wrong.
allocatable() subtracts kube-reserved before packing. Advertised capacity is NOT schedulable:
cpu_reserved_millicores  = min(cpu_total * 0.06, 400)
mem_reserved_mib         = min(mem_total * 0.10, 4096) + 100   (+100 = eviction hard threshold)
max_pods is enforced per instance type because the ENI-based pod cap, not CPU or memory, is
frequently the real binding constraint on small nodes -- ignore it and the bin-packer invents
savings that the scheduler will never deliver.
HOURS_PER_MONTH = 730 (365 * 24 / 12). Never 720.
source: AWS EC2 On-Demand Linux, Asia Pacific (Mumbai), retrieved 2026-08-01

_comment: The honest default for a hand-managed node group. Nothing scales in on its own, so a
right-sizing only saves money once an operator removes a node. Savings are reported as
'unlocks N nodes' -- a capacity headroom claim, NOT a realised bill reduction.
Karpenter consolidates and terminates empty nodes without human action, so a node delta
does become a bill delta. No control-plane surcharge beyond the usual EKS cluster fee.
EKS Auto Mode is Karpenter-equivalent for consolidation but AWS bills a management
surcharge on top of the EC2 price. Applying it matters: a 12% surcharge on the nodes you
KEEP eats part of the saving from the node you removed, so the same right-sizing is worth
measurably less here than under self-managed Karpenter. Reporting the two as one number
would overstate the result.
Every new node the packer opens pays this before a single application pod lands on it.
Seeded onto each node FIRST. Omitting it is the most common way a bin-packing model
produces a node count the cluster can never actually achieve.
Measured from the demo cluster: kube-proxy, CNI, kube-state-metrics node agent,
node-exporter, promtail and KubeThrifty's own cgroup-truth collector.
